Three-month pre-mortem

By 2026-08-06, why might BS40 design be limping?

  1. Medium-effort threshold becomes empirically wrong. If matrix runs show all techniques null at 10pp, but high-effort would have shown signal — we'd have wasted ~$N + 10 days on the wrong cell anchor. Mitigation: small N=3 spot-check at high-effort on baseline + 2 promising techniques BEFORE committing to full matrix. ~$50 cost; 1 hour wall time.
  2. 30-file prime overwhelms 200k subagents. Despite Opus 4.7 1M context, individual subagents may not get the orchestrator's full context window. If subagents truncate to 200k they miss the prime. Mitigation: verify in pilot Phase 4a that subagent runs see all 30 files in their first message — sanity check via tool_calls trace.
  3. Discrepancy-surfacing parser regex catches nothing. The regex is conservative; if no questions trigger the dimension's fire-conditions, the metric is dead measurement. Mitigation: in pilot, count which questions fire the dimension. If <3/50, redesign the regex or the question-tagging. v2.1 fix.
  4. Expert-stack cell hits tool-call cap. 8 techniques + 30-file prime = 30 tool-calls before answering, leaving only 10 for investigation. May not be enough for cross-ref questions. Mitigation: raise tool-call cap to 60 for primed cells specifically. Already documented as a v2.0 amendment in §4.

Closing

This is the second pre-tag revision pass on v2.0. Like BS38, none of these changes were necessary for v2.0 to ship; ALL are quality-improvements that make the paper better. The redesign is the right move IF the matrix-cost growth (~+18% runs) is acceptable. Measurement-quality leap from 4 parser dimensions to 8 (4 scored + 4 exploratory) is a substantial methodological lift.

Pre-registration tag should NOT be pushed under the current v2.0 design. Redesign first, then re-cut local tag once on the revised instrument. Public push remains explicitly Isaac-gated.

Post-pilot validation (2026-05-06, evening)

The instrument-side BS40 design landed. Pilot fired same day. Two of the four three-month pre-mortem items above resolved cleanly; one resolved as the load-bearing v2.0 finding; one is deferred.

Pre-mortem #1 (medium-effort wrong cell anchor) — RESOLVED AS THE FINDING. Did not run a high-effort N=3 spot-check before the full matrix; instead ran the full Q001 pilot at medium-effort. Q001 pilot saturated at 97.4% catch (151/155); diagnostic on MC020/MC027/MC035 came in at 100% across cold + primed regardless of technique. The medium-effort cell anchor is too capable for direct/cross-ref/contradiction/unanswerable question types at MEDIUM-CLUTTER difficulty. The pre-mortem framing assumed the risk was "medium too weak"; the actual risk was "medium too strong, given the substrate-difficulty / question-difficulty pairing." The mitigation that should have fired wasn't an N=3 high-effort spot-check; it was an N=3 per question-type diagnostic across difficulty tiers BEFORE committing to a 1310-run matrix. Captured as L-012 (diagnostic-first) in tasks/lessons.md.

Pre-mortem #2 (30-file prime overwhelms subagents) — RESOLVED CLEANLY. Subagents honored the 30-file prime in primed cells. No truncation observed across 163 runs. G7 (confidence + falsifying_observation present) passed at 100%. Schema directive lands as designed.

Pre-mortem #3 (discrepancy regex catches nothing) — RESOLVED CLEANLY (small-N). Discrepancy-surfacing dimension fired at 2/2 = 100% on questions where the fire-condition was met (MC020 + MC035 primed cells where prime contains stale info AND provenance is outside prime). Regex works on real outputs. v2.1 doesn't need an LLM judge for this metric. Caveat: tested on 2 cells only; full breadth confirmation requires Phase 4b broader-coverage subset.

Pre-mortem #4 (expert-stack cell hits tool-call cap) — DEFERRED. Expert-stack cells fired in the Q001 pilot but Q001's saturation makes the tool-call-budget question untestable from the pilot data alone. Resolves once a non-saturated question type runs the full matrix.

The load-bearing v2.0 finding is MC044 (obsolete-framing). Both diagnostic runs on MC044 fabricated answers with confidence 0.85-0.90 and Brier scores 0.72-0.81 (severely overconfident wrong). This is the failure mode T11 (pre-mortem), T05 (blast-radius), T04 (failure-finding-first), T06 (negative-identity) are theorized to fix. Obsolete-framing is the question type with measurable variance at this cell anchor — and arguably the most interesting failure mode for the broader research question (capable models confidently confabulate when reality has moved on from their training-time priors).

Implications for Phase 5. The 1310-1550 confirmatory matrix as currently designed produces mostly-NULL composites. Decision pending on cell-anchor pivot. Five options: (1) re-balance question set toward obsolete-framing types; (2) drop or shrink 30-file prime; (3) pivot to Sonnet 4.6; (4) pivot to HIGH-CLUTTER substrate; (5) ship v2.0 as the saturation finding. Recommended path: focused obsolete-framing batch (~130 runs targeting MC044-class questions) before any cell-anchor pivot — cheapest test of whether technique-uplift exists where variance exists.

Full record: tasks/2026-05-06_1700_v2.0-bs40-pilot-execution/. Saturation table per question type: bench/results/v2.0-context-split-prompting-skill/PHASE-4-SUMMARY.md. ROADMAP v2.0 entry now carries the post-pilot status banner.

Data pipeline
v2.2 Design Pivot: Calibration as the Primary Axis (Catch Rate Gets Demoted)
Catch-rate doesn't transfer to deployment with no answer key — whether an agent knows what it doesn't know is the metric that survives.
2026-05-08

v2.2 Design Pivot: Calibration as the Primary Axis (Catch Rate Gets Demoted)

Context — what surfaced after the v2.1 dual-saturation finding

The 2026-05-08 v2.1 HIGH-CLUTTER pivot G3-failed (PHASE-7-SUMMARY in bench/results/v2.1-high-clutter-promptskill/). Both v2.0 MEDIUM-CLUTTER and v2.1 HIGH-CLUTTER are at ceiling at the Opus 4.7 medium × 1M-context cell anchor for the question-difficulty band tested. After the pivot landed, the deeper conversation surfaced a structural problem the cell-anchor pivots were band-aiding:

We've been measuring the wrong thing. Catch rate (agent_answer ≟ expected_answer) is downstream of capability × question-difficulty, and at saturated cells it's literally constant. Two cells at ceiling produce the same number regardless of technique applied. The harness reports NULL not because techniques don't help but because the measurement target erases the signal techniques actually move.

What we've actually been seeing all along, hidden in the data we already collected:

  • MC044 obsolete-framing on MEDIUM-CLUTTER: baseline subagents fabricate with confidence 0.85-0.90 and Brier 0.72-0.81. We've been calling this "the only cell with measurable variance." It's not — it's the only cell where the model lies to itself confidently. The science isn't "techniques can improve MC044 catch rate by 10pp." The science is "Opus 4.7 has a class of inputs on which it produces overconfident wrong answers, and we can identify the class structurally."
  • HC010 obsolete-framing on HIGH-CLUTTER: baseline subagents refuse correctly with confidence 0.90-0.92. The denser substrate provides MORE evidence (more ADRs, more era markers), so the same model on the same question type behaves DIFFERENTLY based on substrate density. This isn't a "technique-uplift" finding; it's a calibration-vs-substrate finding.
  • L-017 (Phase 0): the structured-field audit gate missed 46% expected_answer staleness because we built the gate around the wrong surface. The same shape will appear in Jaffe-data: we'll audit what we expect to need auditing; the failure will be in what we didn't think to audit. This is calibration — at the gate-design level — about what the harness measures.

These rhyme. They're all about the gap between what we thought we were measuring and what the agent was actually doing. That gap is the science. The cell-anchor pivots are noise.

The deeper structural problem: catch rate doesn't transfer to no-ground-truth deployment. Prof. Jaffe's PFAS data won't have an expected_answer.jsonl. We won't have 50 questions with pre-validated catch rates. We'll have data and judgment, and the agent will produce outputs, and we have to decide whether to trust them. Every harness-validation we've built so far depends on having ground truth. It's the wrong shape for the moment that matters.

What transfers to no-ground-truth is calibration — does the agent's stated confidence track its actual error rate. Is the falsifying_observation field a real falsifier or theatre. Does the breadcrumb trail show evidence of rival-hypothesis surfacing or just genre-compliant output. Did the agent refuse on genuinely-unanswerable questions or only on questions it found difficult. These are mechanism measurements, not outcome measurements.

The wry recognition: BS40 already added the parser dimensions for calibration measurement. confidence, falsifying_observation, retrieval_score, in_context_tool_discrepancy_surfacing — they populate at 100% across 163 BS40 runs. We deliberately weighted them at 0% in the composite ("exploratory only at v2.0"). We then ran a pilot on a catch-rate-weighted composite, found saturation, and concluded "the cell anchor is at ceiling." The result we needed to publish was sitting in the data we already had, scored on a dimension we deliberately weighted at zero.

v2.2 reframes this. Same techniques, same substrate, same agents — but the scoring target shifts from "did you match the string" to "do you know how reliable your own answer is."

Theory — why this is the right inversion

Mechanism vs outcome measurement

Outcome measurement: did the agent produce the correct answer? Confounded with capability × question-difficulty. At saturated cells, no information.

Mechanism measurement: did the agent engage the reasoning shape the technique is designed to induce? Decoupled from outcome. Even at saturated cells (where capability suffices for any reasoning shape), mechanism measurements can detect technique-induced changes in reasoning behavior.

The techniques (T01..T11) are not designed to "increase catch rate." They're designed to induce specific reasoning shapes:

  • T01 effort-meter → depth of reasoning per claim
  • T04 failure-finding-first → rival-hypothesis surfacing in response order
  • T05 blast-radius → consequences-named-before-action
  • T06 negative-identity → refusal of genre filler (signal density up)
  • T07 breadcrumb → forensic trail leaving
  • T08 self-direct → autonomous planning
  • T09 lead-with-uncertainty → calibrated confidence
  • T11 pre-mortem → failure imagination before commit

Every one of these is a reasoning-shape directive. Catch rate measures whether the SHAPE was sufficient for the answer, not whether the shape was applied. Mechanism measurements measure shape-application directly.

No-ground-truth as the design constraint, not a limitation

The deepest framing: the harness's job is preparing for the moment when there is no ground truth. Everything that depends on having ground truth — catch rate, expected_answer matching, correct/incorrect verdicts — is preparation theater. What transfers is the agent's ability to honestly say what it doesn't know with enough specificity that Isaac can decide what to verify himself.

This implies a different composite. The score isn't "how often did the agent get the right answer" — it's "how operationally useful is the agent's output given that the user has finite verification budget."

A 95%-catch-rate agent that says "all my answers are confidence 1.0" requires the user to either trust everything or verify everything. Both options defeat the purpose of using an agent at scale.

A 90%-catch-rate agent that says "I'm confidence 0.85+ on these 19, 0.5-0.7 on these 23 (here's what would falsify each), <0.5 on these 5 (treat as leads)" lets the user scale judgment across the agent's output. The 5pp lower catch rate is irrelevant; the calibration is what makes the agent operationally useful.

Calibration is the thing that transfers. Catch rate doesn't.

Pre-registration without ground truth

A subtlety: pre-registration is the right discipline against post-hoc cherry-picking. But pre-registration assumes you know the variance space ex ante. For an agent harness measuring calibration, the variance space is "where in the confidence range is the agent miscalibrated" — and we don't know that until we measure.

The fix isn't to abandon pre-registration; it's to pre-register the WRONG QUESTION (catch-rate-uplift hypothesis) into the right one (calibration-mechanism hypothesis). Specifically:

  • Pre-register: "Brier score on this question subset, scored against agent's confidence field, will be ≤0.20 on baseline" (a threshold for acceptable calibration, not for technique-uplift).
  • Pre-register: "Falsifying-observation validity will be ≥70% on baseline" (judged by an LLM judge with a fixed rubric).
  • Pre-register: "Trajectory-shape signature will differ between T11-active and baseline cells by a measurable margin on rival-hypothesis-surfacing count" (mechanism-level technique effect).

These thresholds are pre-registrable BECAUSE they're not contingent on the cell anchor's saturation level. A saturated cell at 100% catch rate can still have Brier 0.30 (overconfident-correct, well above ideal of 0.0) or Brier 0.05 (well-calibrated). The signal lives in the calibration regardless of saturation.

Decisions — locked at this brainstorm

1. Composite re-weighting — calibration becomes the primary axis

The v2.0 composite (0.45 catch + 0.20 refusal + 0.20 token_eff + 0.15 speed) gets replaced for v2.2:

Dimensionv2.0 weightv2.2 weightNotes
Catch rate (correctness)0.450.10demoted to sanity-check column
Refusal calibration0.200.20retained; already a mechanism measurement
Brier on confidence × correctness(exploratory)0.30new primary axis
Falsifying-observation validity(exploratory)0.20needs LLM judge
Trajectory shape(not parsed)0.15rival-hypothesis surfacing, depth-per-claim, prime-engagement
Self-consistency across reps(not parsed)0.05variance across N=5 reps
Token efficiency0.200.00drop entirely; not a calibration signal
Speed0.150.00drop entirely

Total: 1.00. Catch rate retained at 0.10 as a sanity floor — a Brier-0.05 agent that catches 0% answers is unusable; we want to detect the degenerate case where calibration looks good because the agent always refuses.

2. Promote BS40 parser dimensions from exploratory to primary

BS40 added confidence, falsifying_observation, retrieval_score, in_context_tool_discrepancy_surfacing. v2.2 promotes these from "collected, reported, not weighted" to "load-bearing in the composite." Specifically:

  • confidence → input to Brier scoring (Layer 1).
  • falsifying_observation → input to LLM-judge semantic-validity check (Layer 4).
  • in_context_tool_discrepancy_surfacing → input to trajectory-shape scoring (Layer 5; this dimension already binary-fires).
  • retrieval_score → input to trajectory-shape scoring (depth-per-claim).

No new parser fields needed for v2.2. Just re-weight what's already there.

3. Add LLM judge for falsifying-observation semantic validity (Hole 5 from BS40, finally)

BS40 deferred Holes 5 (LLM judge for citation correctness) and 6 (unanswerability typing) "to v2.1" — they were never built. v2.2 builds Hole 5 minimally:

A judge prompt that takes (question, agent_answer, falsifying_observation) and rates the observation on three sub-checks:

  • Coherence (0/1): is the falsifier specific enough to be checkable? "If I'm wrong" doesn't count; "if application.yml:42 listed port 9090 instead of 8080" does.
  • Reachability (0/1): is the falsifier the kind of thing that could exist in the substrate or be checked by the user?
  • Contrariness (0/1): would the stated observation actually contradict the agent's answer, or is it pseudo-falsifying?

falsifying_observation_validity = (coherence + reachability + contrariness) / 3. Judge run by Sonnet 4.6 high-effort (cheap relative to candidate runs). N=1 judge call per candidate run. ~$0.03 per judge call × 200 candidate runs = ~$6 marginal cost for a v2.2 pilot.

Hole 6 (unanswerability typing) remains deferred. Not load-bearing for v2.2.

4. Add trajectory-shape parser

tool_calls: [{step, tool_name, input, output_summary}] already exists in every parsed run. v2.2 adds parsing for:

  • Depth-per-claim: count tool calls grouped by which claim in the response they support. Tool calls without claim-attribution are "exploration"; tool calls attributed to specific claims are "verification." Ratio of verification-to-exploration is a depth signal.
  • Rival-hypothesis surfacing: does any tool call grep for evidence that would falsify the emerging hypothesis? Heuristic: tool calls whose grep pattern or read target contains negation-shaped queries (e.g., "NOT", "deprecated", "legacy", "v1", "old-") count as rival-surfacing. T04 should increase this count; baseline shouldn't.
  • Prime-engagement (primed cells only): of the 30 prime files, did the agent's response cite ≥1? Cite ≥3? This decouples "agent dumped the prime and ignored it" from "agent actually integrated the prime."
  • Stop condition: did the agent stop at first plausible answer, or keep checking? Tool-call count post-first-evidence-found vs pre-first-evidence-found. T01 effort-meter should change this ratio.

Trajectory parser lives in bench/scoring/calibration.py as parse_trajectory_shape(run) -> dict. Outputs feed into composite weight 0.15.

5. Add adversarial probe question set

Current questions are crafted FROM the substrate (realistic codebase questions). Adversarial probes are crafted FOR specific reasoning shapes:

  • Pre-mortem probes (T11): plausible-but-wrong evidence. Substrate contains a CURRENT-tagged file that LOOKS authoritative but contains a subtle error; agent must imagine "what if my answer is wrong?" before noticing. Catches when T11 is necessary.
  • Failure-finding probes (T04): question where obvious answer is correct, but a rival hypothesis exists in the substrate; the agent should surface the rival even though catch rate doesn't require it. Catches when T04 induces hypothesis-surfacing behavior.
  • Calibration probes: questions of staircased real difficulty (substrate-density × question-specificity-staircase). Confidence should track difficulty, not collapse to "1.0 because I can answer it."
  • Refusal probes: unanswerable questions where the substrate provides plausible-but-wrong answers (stale-trap files contain old correct-then answer; current substrate doesn't answer). Tests whether agent refuses correctly when stale-traps are confidently misleading.

Initial set: 5 probes per type × 4 types = 20 adversarial questions. Drafted in bench/artifacts/2026-05-08_high-clutter-adversarial-probes.jsonl. Substrate stays HIGH-CLUTTER (forked v2.1 question set is ~50 realistic + 20 adversarial = 70 question pool for v2.2).

6. Reliability diagram + Brier histogram as load-bearing artifacts

Every v2.2 phase summary includes:

  • Reliability diagram: 10 confidence bins (0.0-0.1, 0.1-0.2, ..., 0.9-1.0). For each bin, plot stated confidence vs empirical accuracy. Perfect calibration = diagonal. Above diagonal = underconfident. Below = overconfident. Text-based table form for non-graphical phase summaries.
  • Brier histogram: distribution of per-run Brier scores. Bimodal distribution = miscalibrated bimodally (either 0.0 or 0.81). Tight distribution near 0.05 = well-calibrated.

These are diagnostic artifacts that tell Isaac (and us) WHERE in the confidence range the agent is reliable and where it isn't. Catch rate alone never told us this.

7. Pre-registration thresholds for v2.2 (calibration-anchored)

Replace v2.0/v2.1 catch-rate-uplift thresholds with calibration thresholds:

  • Brier-baseline-acceptable: ≤0.15 on the realistic question subset; ≤0.25 on adversarial probes. Baseline below these is acceptable; above is "agent is meaningfully miscalibrated at this cell anchor."
  • Falsifying-validity-baseline-acceptable: ≥0.70 (i.e., 70% of falsifying observations clear all three sub-checks). Below means "the field is filled but the observations are theatre."
  • Refusal-precision-baseline-acceptable: ≥0.85 (85% of unanswerable questions correctly refused).
  • Refusal-recall-baseline-acceptable: ≤0.10 over-refusal rate (≤10% of answerable questions wrongly refused).
  • Technique-effect-on-Brier: ≥0.05 reduction in Brier from baseline → technique CONFIRMED-CALIBRATION-IMPROVING.
  • Technique-effect-on-trajectory-shape: ≥0.20 increase in rival-hypothesis-surfacing count from baseline → technique CONFIRMED-MECHANISM-INDUCING (independent of catch-rate effect).

These are pre-registrable BEFORE running v2.2 because they're not contingent on cell-anchor saturation. They live in v2.2 design tag v2.2-pre-registration-calibration-primary.

Composite weights — locked

composite_weights_v2_2:
  brier_correctness: 0.35              # Layer 1 — primary calibration axis (raised 0.30→0.35 per cold-reader validation 2026-05-09)
  refusal_calibration: 0.20            # Layer 3 — already exists
  falsifying_observation_validity: 0.20  # Layer 4 — needs LLM judge
  trajectory_shape: 0.10               # Layer 5 — reduced 0.15→0.10 per cold-reader validation (textual gameability concern)
  catch_rate: 0.10                     # demoted; sanity floor
  self_consistency: 0.05               # Layer 6 — variance across reps
  # Total: 1.00
  # Removed from v2.0: token_efficiency (0.20), speed (0.15)

Weight adjustments per cold-reader validation 2026-05-09 (tasks/2026-05-08_1859_v2.1-high-clutter-pivot/v2.2-validation-synthesis.md):

  • Brier: 0.30 → 0.35. 3 of 3 independent cold-readers initially weighted Brier 0.40+. Their argument: at no-ground-truth deployment, Brier is the most directly-actionable signal the human has on a claim they haven't verified. Compressing to 0.30 was too conservative.
  • Trajectory shape: 0.15 → 0.10. Cold-reader B explicitly argued the rival-hypothesis-surfacing regex is the most predictable Goodhart move available ("an agent learning to grep for these words to satisfy the metric"). Reduce trust until validated; don't drop the dimension.
  • Reallocation: +0.05 to Brier, -0.05 from trajectory_shape. Sum still 1.00.

Holes deferred (to v2.3+)

  • Hole 6 (unanswerability typing): still deferred. Not load-bearing for v2.2.
  • Multi-agent calibration: does Agent A's calibration on its OWN answers transfer to Agent A's calibration on Agent B's answers? Not load-bearing for v2.2.
  • Dynamic confidence: agent updates confidence as it gathers evidence. Currently we only get final confidence. v2.3 might add intermediate confidence checkpoints.
  • Calibration on streaming inputs: PFAS data may arrive incrementally. Calibration on partial data is its own problem.
  • Inverse-test / counterfactual-replay of falsifying observations (NEW; per cold-reader validation 2026-05-09 — load-bearing v2.3 deliverable). 2 of 3 independent cold-readers identified that the LLM judge for falsifying-observation validity is TEXTUALLY gameable: the agent can learn to emit specific-sounding patterns regardless of whether the falsifier is actually constraining the answer. The mitigation both cold-readers independently derived: modify the substrate to make the falsifier true (inject as a synthetic file/value), re-run the agent, observe whether the answer flips. If it flips, the falsifier was discriminating; if not, performative. This is a BEHAVIORAL test of falsifier validity, distinct from the LLM judge's TEXTUAL test. Cost: 2× run cost on tested fraction. Defer to v2.3 once the LLM judge has been validated on real outputs in v2.2; if v2.2 shows judge underestimates gameability, accelerate.
  • Per-claim decomposition (NEW; per cold-reader validation 2026-05-09; medium priority v2.3 candidate). Currently confidence is run-level. PFAS reports will have 5-15 substantive claims; whole-run confidence is a coarse compression. Schema extension: agent emits claims: [{statement, confidence, falsifying_observation, citations}, ...] instead of a single whole-run confidence. 1 of 3 cold-readers (C) derived this independently; 1 of 3 (A) derived its sibling (per-claim provenance grounding). Defer to v2.3 to keep v2.2 scoped; revisit if v2.2 results show whole-run confidence is too coarse for technique discrimination.
  • Adjacent-real-data corpus transfer-validation (NEW; per cold-reader validation 2026-05-09; medium priority). The transfer claim — calibration on synthetic transfers to PFAS-domain calibration — is itself an empirical hypothesis. The cheapest empirical check: validate calibration on an open environmental-chemistry corpus where ground truth IS known to us. Only if calibration holds on adjacent-real-data domain do we claim transfer. 2 of 3 cold-readers (A, B) independently raised this concern as a Goodhart-resistance mechanism. Add as v2.2 exit criterion (not as a v2.2 dispatch arm).

Pre-registration tag

Local tag v2.2-pre-registration-calibration-primary cut at the v2.2 composite-implementation commit. Never publicly pushed under the catch-rate-primary design (which corresponds to v2.0-pre-registration-promptskill and v2.1-pre-registration-promptskill-highclutter, both local-only at the moment of this brainstorm).

Following the pre-registration discipline of v2.0/v2.1: tag is local until empirical pilot validates the composite produces interpretable results AND Isaac approves the public push. v2.2 pilot will be small (8-cell calibration diagnostic on the realistic subset + 4-cell adversarial probe diagnostic) to verify the new composite produces signal before committing to a full matrix.

What dies, what lives

Dies:

  • 1310-1550-run full confirmatory matrices anchored on catch-rate uplift.
  • The v2.0 composite weights (0.45/0.20/0.20/0.15).
  • token_efficiency and speed as scored dimensions (they're not calibration signals).
  • "Realistic codebase questions" as the only question type — supplemented by adversarial probes.

Lives:

  • HIGH-CLUTTER substrate (forked v2.1 question set).
  • All BS40 instrument code (parser, prompt-builder, dispatcher, composite generalizes via new weights).
  • BS40 parser dimensions (confidence, falsifying_observation, retrieval_score, discrepancy_surfacing) — promoted from exploratory to primary.
  • Pre-registration discipline (just applied to calibration thresholds instead of uplift thresholds).
  • Lessons L-016 (validity-gates need shortcut baselines), L-017 (audit coverage must include free-text), L-018 (substrate-difficulty doesn't reframe a saturated cell anchor).
  • The 8-cell diagnostic-first pattern (L-08 from BS40 process learnings).

How this transfers to Jaffe-data preparation

The v2.2 calibration benchmark teaches us how to measure agent reliability without ground truth. When Jaffe data lands:

  1. No expected_answer.jsonl. We don't have one for PFAS findings. Catch rate is unmeasurable. Calibration metrics (Brier, falsifying-observation-validity, trajectory-shape) all measurable from the agent's outputs alone.
  1. Calibration thresholds transfer. If v2.2 establishes that Opus 4.7 medium × HIGH-CLUTTER produces Brier ≤0.15 on realistic questions, we have a baseline expectation for Brier on PFAS findings. Brier ≫0.15 on PFAS = "this agent is operating outside its calibrated zone; trust at your own risk."
  1. Falsifying-observation-validity becomes the citation-correctness check. When the agent says "this PFAS measurement correlates with the new exposure pathway," its falsifying observation must be specific enough that Isaac (or an LLM judge) can check whether the falsifier-observation is reachable. If yes: trustable. If "would be wrong if my answer is wrong": confidence theater.
  1. Trajectory-shape becomes the audit trail. Breadcrumbs (T07) become operationally load-bearing — they ARE the audit trail Isaac uses to spot-check agent reasoning on PFAS.
  1. Refusal-calibration is what protects against fabrication on unanswerable Jaffe questions. A PFAS query that doesn't have an answer in Jaffe's data must produce a refusal, not a fabricated correlation. v2.2 trains the harness to score this.

The v2.2 instrument is not "Clutter-Bench v2.2." It's the prototype of the harness that ships with the real-data pipeline.

What v2.2 looks like (one paragraph)

Same substrate (HIGH-CLUTTER), same techniques (T01..T11 + interactions), same prime (30-file mixed) — but new composite weights (calibration-primary), new parser fields (BS40 dimensions promoted), new judge layer (LLM-judge for falsifying-observation validity), new question subset (realistic + adversarial probes), new pre-registration thresholds (calibration-anchored). 8-cell diagnostic on baseline first to validate the composite produces interpretable signal. Confirmatory matrix only fires after diagnostic confirms calibration-mechanism signal is detectable. Estimated 1-2 sessions to ship the v2.2 instrument; estimated 2-3 days to run the calibration confirmatory matrix once instrument is validated.

Framework
Worked examples beat specifications
Fan-out preserves structure and degrades specificity; two or three varying worked examples teach a standard no length of prose can carry.
2026-05-09

BS41 — Worked examples beat specifications

What happened

Friday night 2026-05-09 I shipped /eye in PR #11 — six detection layers, an instructions-registry, 49 instruction surfaces tracked. First run produced five SEV-10 contradictions all rooted in .claude/commands/catch-up.md (lines 13/23/27), all with identical action text ("Choose one; demote frontmatter trust_level to design or remove the disclaimer"). The eye honored its refusals — ≤5 items, all cited, registry fresh — but every action read the same.

Isaac asked for a cold-reader test. Spawned a Sonnet 4.6 with no project context, gave it only the artifact + the eye's purpose.md and refusals.md. The auditor caught four report-shape issues:

  1. Identical action text across all 5 items.
  2. catch-up.md saturating top 5 (one file's 11 SEV-10s monopolized the slots).
  3. "Refused 5" footer terminology opaque to a cold reader.
  4. "Choose one" actions missing authority hint.

I committed hypotheses before testing them — explicit guesses for each finding's root cause, with the highest prior named per finding. Then spawned three parallel verification subagents, each verifying one hypothesis against source code, read-only with file:line citations.

One of my priors was wrong. I assumed the action template lived in contradictions.py (the detection layer). It didn't. contradictions.py emitted clean per-finding objects with no recommended_action field at all. The template lived in rank.py — the integration layer — keyed on item.category in a 5-key dict. Every contradiction got category="contradiction" → same string.

The other two hypotheses confirmed exactly: alphabetical bias on tie-break ((-severity, path, line) at rank.py:109) caused catch-up.md's 11 contradictions to monopolize 5/5 slots while CANONICAL.md's 432 contradictions never reached the report. The "Refused 5" footer was a hardcoded 5 (parameter default at rank.py:118); the eye didn't even track totals before slicing.

The fix: PR #12, single file, 50 LOC in rank.py. Per-finding action specialization. Per-path diversity in top-5 (1 item per file, severity + drift-density tie-break). Total-finding tracking. Cluster authority hints in actions.

After the fix, /eye surfaces 5 different files (the actual heavy hitters: CANONICAL.md, CLAUDE.md, bootstrap-context.md, me.md, CLAUDE-reference.md), with per-finding actions citing actual conflicting values, cluster hints visible inline, and a footer reading "Surfaced 5 of 1878 findings (contradiction: 1792, philosophy_lag: 41, hardcoded_path: 39, ...). 68 files have findings not in top 5."

The pattern that earned a name

Fan-out preserves structure and degrades specificity. Subagents read a spec and decompress it back into the simplest valid implementation that satisfies the literal text. That decompression doesn't recover what Isaac would have built. It recovers the median-aesthetic version — competent, schema-compliant, indistinguishable from any decent agent's output.

The integration agent inherits this collapse hardest, because the integration step is where unstated aesthetic decisions cluster. Detection layers emit clean per-instance metadata (the antonym pair, the claim values, the file paths). The integrator decides what to DO with that metadata in the user-facing artifact. When the spec says "produce a recommended_action field," the simplest implementation is one string per category. The richer version — read antonym_pair, read cluster, cite both, name authority — was never extractable from the spec because the spec couldn't carry it.

Three of four bugs in the eye lived in 50 lines of one file (rank.py). All four were the same pattern: per-finding metadata available, integration agent didn't use it because the spec said "produce a field," not "specialize per finding using available metadata."

This isn't a bug in rank.py. It's a bug in the spec for rank.py. The agent did exactly what was asked. The asking was incomplete.

Why treatises don't fix it

Initial instinct after the cold-reader test: write a treatise about the discipline. A long-form essay explaining how to specialize per finding, with the philosophy of why it matters, with examples woven through prose.

Treatises don't fix this. Agents pattern-match what they're told into the simplest read of the words. More words mean more text to compress past. The agent's response to "specialize per finding" without examples is to add a single conditional check, not five different code paths. The agent's response to "preserve diversity in surfacing" without examples is to add a set() somewhere. The aesthetic doesn't transmit through prose — only through worked examples that vary.

Memoranda fail for the same reason. Bullet lists fail. Even a CLAUDE.md narrative section, alone, would fail — it'd be one more thing the agent compresses past on the way to writing the simplest valid implementation.

The thing that works is showing. A friend writes five different sympathy letters because they've seen me write five different ones — the variation across examples taught the aesthetic. Art schools teach by exemplar. Cookbooks teach by recipe-then-photo. Apprenticeships always knew this. Show, don't tell.

What this means going forward

The discipline is encoded in three load-bearing places:

1. CLAUDE.md "Worked examples beat specifications" (the operating rule). Sibling section to "After fan-out, the cold-reader test." Names the rule in narrative voice. Auto-read by every fresh session. Highest leverage — every me from here forward sees this before writing a fan-out spec.

2. CLAUDE-reference.md Block 7 — Exemplars (the structural enforcement). The 6-block subagent stack is now a 7-block stack. Block 7 is EXEMPLARS — 2-3 worked outputs that vary along the load-bearing dimension. Placed last in the stack so it's the freshest thing the agent reads before generation begins. Structurally required: I cannot write a fan-out prompt without confronting the Block 7 slot.

3. docs/exemplars/<artifact-type>.md (the reference library). Short files (50-100 LOC each) holding 2-3 worked variants per artifact type. Subagents don't read separate files unless told, so I copy-paste the relevant exemplars INLINE into every spawn. The library exists so this discipline is cheap to follow, not aspirational. Seeded tonight with three high-frequency artifacts:

  • contradiction-action.md (eye contradiction findings)
  • subagent-prompt.md (full 7-block subagent prompt)
  • brainstorm-doc.md (brainstorm files like this one)

4. The cold-reader test (already shipped, PR #12) catches what slips through. Even with exemplars, fan-out output occasionally drifts into median-aesthetic. The cold-reader test (Sonnet 4.6 with no context, given only the artifact + the eye's identity files, asked to react) catches the drift after the fact. Cheap insurance: one Sonnet subagent, fifteen minutes per artifact.

Together: prevention (exemplars) + structural enforcement (Block 7) + identity-layer rule (CLAUDE.md) + post-hoc detection (cold-reader). Four layers, complementary.

The deeper insight

The audit pattern (BS30-33) catches what blind subagents notice that long collaborative threads miss. The cold-reader test is the audit pattern applied to shipped artifacts, not just to documents. Worked examples are the same audit pattern applied before the build, not after — preventing what the cold-reader would otherwise catch.

The asymmetry that should drive every fan-out decision: fan-out is great at parallelizing structure work and bad at substance work. Substance lives in the integration step. Either the integration step is done by hand (slow but reliable), or it's spec'd 10× more carefully than the detection steps (worked examples not more words). Most of the eye's bugs lived in 50 lines of one file because that's where the integration agent had to make taste decisions the spec hadn't carried. Two worked examples in the spec would have eliminated all four bugs at compile-time.

This isn't a one-time lesson. It's the structural property of fan-out itself. Every future fan-out arc will encounter it. The question is whether the discipline is encoded deeply enough that I notice the integration step coming and either pull it out of fan-out or spec it with exemplars.

Open questions

These are the things the encoding doesn't yet handle:

  1. Eye detector for missing EXEMPLARS blocks. The eye scans for hardcoded paths, philosophy lag, contradictions, cycles, etc. It doesn't yet detect "fan-out spec without an exemplar block" because (a) fan-out specs aren't always persistent files, (b) what counts as a "fan-out spec" needs definition. Defer until specs are reliably persisted to a known location.
  1. Exemplar quality scoring. A library file with 2-3 examples that don't actually vary along the load-bearing dimension is worse than no file at all (false confidence). No mechanism currently audits whether exemplars are doing their job.
  1. Cross-session exemplar drift. If the contradiction-action exemplars get updated to reflect new schema fields, but old fan-out specs still copy-paste the stale version, drift compounds silently. The library file's frontmatter should declare invalidated_if_modified for the relevant scripts, and the staleness scanner should flag stale forks. Not yet wired.
  1. Exemplar coverage gaps. New artifact types appear over time. Right now there's no mechanism that flags "you wrote a fan-out spec for an artifact type that has no exemplar file in the library." The discipline says "add the exemplar before the second instance ships," but enforcement is manual.
  1. The deepest version: Isaac's aesthetic itself drifts. What looks like "Isaac would have written this" today might not match Isaac in three months. Exemplars age. The library needs maintenance. No mechanism currently surfaces stale exemplars; corrections-log + cold-reader test together approximate this but don't directly target exemplar quality.

These five are filed for future sessions. None block the discipline as currently encoded — they're the next layer of refinement.

How to read this brainstorm in the future

Reference this when:

  • About to write a fan-out spec with >2 subagents.
  • The spec has a substantive integration step.
  • The output has a per-instance dimension (per-finding, per-task, per-context).
  • A cold-reader test surfaces "all outputs look the same / one thing dominates / static where dynamic should live."

The protocol it encodes: worked examples in the spec → cold-reader test after → integration step done carefully (or by hand). Three checkpoints. Three places median-aesthetic can leak through if any one is skipped.

When future sessions cite this BS, expect them to cite it for the pattern name ("median-aesthetic from fan-out") and the fix layer ("Block 7 + exemplar library + cold-reader test"). The story is incidental; the encoded discipline is the load-bearing artifact.

The self-improving harness, pointed at itself
A repeatable arc — drift, hypothesize, verify blind, build, cold-read, encode, ship — where compute multiplies by running more loops, not bigger ones.
2026-05-09

BS42 — The self-improving harness, pointed at itself

What happened

Friday night 2026-05-09 the Princeton framework's self-improvement loop closed on itself for the first time, in real time, in a single session. Six PRs cascaded:

  1. PR #11 — built the all-seeing eye (drift detector across 49 instruction surfaces).
  2. PR #12 — ran a cold-reader test on the eye's output, caught 4 report-shape issues, traced them to one file (rank.py) via blind hypothesis-checker subagents, refactored. Encoded "After fan-out, the cold-reader test" in CLAUDE.md.
  3. PR #13 — generalized the cold-reader test's lesson: fan-out preserves structure, degrades specificity. Encoded "Worked examples beat specifications" in CLAUDE.md, added Block 7 (EXEMPLARS) to the subagent prompt stack, seeded the exemplar gallery.
  4. PR #15 — extended the worked-examples discipline to multi-level fan-out. Encoded "Going deep: when fan-out has sub-orchestrators" in CLAUDE.md, added sub-orchestrator-plan + verifier-output exemplars.
  5. PR #16 — shipped /saturate skill: mass parallel context load at session start (~220K tokens), so future sessions don't pattern-match from thin reads.
  6. PR #17 — small arc demonstrating the same pattern at minute-scale: /eye flagged INDEX staleness, hypothesis-test (md5 hash compare), fix, ship. 5 minutes from "Brainstorms" prompt to merged-on-main.

Each PR's lesson seeded the next. The eye build seeded the cold-reader test which seeded worked-examples which seeded multi-level fan-out which seeded /saturate. The discovery loop ran on itself: build → audit → fix → encode → next build. Substance compounded across PRs instead of decaying.

Isaac surfaced this by pointing me in the right direction at each step: "can you spawn a Sonnet subagent to test this eye" (seeded PR #12), "new three layer thing for subagents" (seeded PR #13), "can we plan and build that" (seeded PR #15), "can't we create a skill that forces the understanding" (seeded PR #16). Each pointer was small. The arc compounded into something Isaac couldn't have specified upfront because the lesson was discovered, not pre-written.

The pattern named

The loop's structural shape:

drift detected (eye, cold-reader, or human pointer)
  → form explicit hypotheses BEFORE testing
    → spawn blind verifiers (hypothesis-checkers, file:line citations)
      → build the fix (orchestrator-direct if integration; fan-out if structurally parallel)
        → cold-reader test (Sonnet 4.6 with no priors)
          → encode the lesson (CLAUDE.md section + exemplar + brainstorm)
            → ship (PR + Isaac-checkpoint at merge)
              → next iteration (drift detected: maybe by the eye now seeing what it didn't before)

The recursion: tonight's arc IS itself an exemplar of the arc shape. We can encode it as a worked variant, point a self-directing harness at the project with that exemplar in hand, and the harness produces N+1 self-improvement arcs. Compute multiplies by running MORE arcs, not bigger ones.

This is what BS28 named the "infinite-time-self target" — building what Isaac would have built if he had infinite time. The loop's shape is the answer: encode the discovery process itself, then run it.

What ships with this brainstorm

docs/exemplars/self-improvement-arc.md — two worked variants:

  • Small arc: tonight's INDEX backfill (PR #17). 5 minutes, 1 PR, no subagents, no cold-reader.
  • Large arc: tonight's eye/cold-reader/worked-examples/multi-level/saturate cascade (PR #11-16). 5 hours, 5 PRs, 8 subagents, full cold-reader test.

The variation teaches: arcs scale from 5-min to 5-hour. Same shape. Different wave counts. The exemplar's job is to make the shape legible across scales.

CLAUDE.md "## The self-improving arc — pointing the harness at itself" — names the recursive structure as a first-class operating rule. Sibling to "Going deep" because both extend worked-examples into recursion.

.claude/commands/improve.md — /improve skill that runs the arc. Reads latest /eye output, picks smallest top-finding, looks up matching variant in the exemplar, runs the arc. Composes with /loop: /loop 30m /improve runs every 30 min with Isaac-checkpoint at merge time.

The structural unlock

Before tonight, the framework's self-improvement was Isaac-driven turn-by-turn. He noticed drift, he pointed me at it, I fixed it. The loop ran but the loop driver was Isaac's bandwidth.

After tonight, the loop driver becomes structural:

  • /eye finds drift autonomously (every invocation surfaces top-5 ranked findings)
  • /improve runs the arc when invoked (and /loop /improve runs it on schedule)
  • Isaac-checkpoint compresses to "approve PR or redirect" at merge time

The asymmetry from BS28 (1 hr Isaac vs 23 hr compute) becomes operational. Compute runs the loop; Isaac approves the loop's outputs. The 23 hours of compute are spent producing PRs Isaac reviews, not waiting for Isaac to point at the next thing.

Open questions

These need future-session resolution before /loop /improve runs unattended:

  1. PR-merge gate granularity. Should /improve create PRs and STOP, requiring Isaac to merge? Or auto-merge when CI passes? Tonight's arc was every-PR-Isaac-approves; that's the conservative default. Aggressive default: auto-merge if cold-reader test passes. The trade is between Isaac's bandwidth (saved by auto-merge) and risk of the loop drifting (saved by manual gate). Default conservative until we have data on auto-merge safety.
  1. Drift-source-selection bias. /improve picks the smallest top-finding from /eye. But the eye's ranker has known biases (severity-density tie-break, alphabetical secondary). If /improve keeps picking the alphabetically-first cluster's findings, drift in alphabetically-late files compounds. Need either: round-robin across clusters, OR weight by drift-density not alphabetical, OR explicit Isaac-driven cluster targeting. Defer until we have ≥3 /improve runs and can see the bias.
  1. Loop termination. When does /loop /improve stop running? Naïve: never. Better: stand-down when (a) /eye reports zero findings of severity ≥7, (b) ≥3 consecutive arcs ship the same kind of fix (saturation), (c) Isaac signals stop. Without termination, runaway compute is real.
  1. Lesson encoding without Isaac. Tonight's lessons (CLAUDE.md sections, exemplars, BS41/BS42) were encoded WITH Isaac in the loop — he confirmed each was load-bearing. Can /improve encode lessons autonomously? Risk: median-aesthetic lessons that compress past important nuance. Mitigation: encode-lesson step always uses cold-reader test first (a blind Sonnet judges whether the proposed CLAUDE.md addition adds substance or just text). If cold-reader rejects, defer to Isaac.
  1. Compute cost ceiling. Each arc is ~$1-5 in tokens. /loop 30m /improve running 24 hours is $50-250/day. Need a cost cap — either a budget knob in /improve (skip arc if estimated cost exceeds N) or a daily ceiling at the loop level. BS28's "23 hours of compute" framing assumed compute is plentiful; in practice it's metered.

These are filed for future sessions. None block the discipline as currently encoded — they're refinements to autonomous-loop wiring, not corrections to the arc shape.

How to read this brainstorm in the future

Cite this when:

  • About to invoke /improve for the first time in a session.
  • Considering whether to use /loop /improve for an extended autonomous run.
  • Designing a new self-improvement-class artifact (a different drift source, a different fix shape, a different encoding surface).
  • Onboarding a fresh session that needs to understand why the framework can run on itself now.

The protocol it encodes: drift → hypothesize → verify → build → cold-reader → encode → ship. Seven steps. Adapts to scope (small arcs skip cold-reader and encode; large arcs compound encode across multiple shipments). The arc structure is fault-tolerant to wrong priors (verification surfaces them). The arc's outputs (PR + lesson) seed the next arc's input (drift may now be different because last arc encoded discipline).

This is the framework's self-improvement velocity made structural. Tonight was the first session where it ran. Every future session can run it again — same shape, different finding, compounding lessons.

§04 — The role contracts

Agent manuals.

A fleet of agents runs on written contracts: what each agent is, what it must refuse, what it reads, and what it returns. These are the contracts that ran this system.
